title: One coherent reference removed known input mixing from circuit-ratio tests in fully observed linear models
abstract: We tested a repair for coherent input spread in a circuit-ratio method. In a fully observed stable linear model, n known independent mixed input directions and one known coherent reference recover the transfer matrix up to one scalar from rank-one spectral differences. Input powers and response phases can be unknown. This applies standard projective-frame reconstruction. It removes known input mixing before a four-edge ratio cancels scalar cell filters and separate source and target gains. In 90 exact model checks on two adult worm maps and one selected MICrONS mouse graph, the largest relative ratio error was 2.05e-15. A matched sample and mean-power benchmark had 960 paired trials in twelve fixed synthetic circuits. At 196608 independent spectral samples and dose 16, corrected median errors were 0.0150 and 0.0191 for 8 and 16 states, versus 0.0129 and 0.0176 for ideal single-node inputs. A weak reference term raised error. An unknown common input map passed all direction checks in a stable DC example while changing the ratio by 47.4 percent. We give proofs, conditional error bounds, original code, synthetic evidence, aggregate graph checks and exact external-input hashes. Known neural-current input directions, fixed dynamics and background, scalar filters and full observation are required. No measured neural activity was fitted. External database records and matrices are excluded.
